title: My Appeal to Nirmala Sitharaman Ji on LTCG & STT - Rahul Jain
creator: Rahul Jain
summary: Rahul Jain makes a direct appeal to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, who had invited debate on long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) and securities transaction tax (STT), tracing 22 years of Indian market taxation. Before October 2004 there was LTCG at 10% without indexation and 20% with it, short-term gains at slab rates, no STT and tax-free dividends. In 2004 P. Chidambaram scrapped LTCG to 0% and introduced STT — because FIIs using the Mauritius treaty paid no LTCG — but STT then rose in 2005 and 2006, short-term tax rose to 15% in 2008, and after cuts in 2012–13 taxes rose again from 2016: dividend tax, LTCG restored at 10% in 2018 while STT stayed — a broken promise, he argues — dividends taxed at slab from 2020, and in July 2024 LTCG raised to 12.5% and short-term tax to 20%, with further STT hikes in October 2024 and April 2026. STT collections rose from about ₹11,500 crore in FY19 to about ₹57,000 crore in FY26; with 13 revisions in 22 years the regime is unstable, and taxes plus rupee depreciation erode FII returns. His proposals: scrap LTCG if STT stays, cap STT, make LTCG 0% after three years, raise the exemption from ₹1.25 lakh to about ₹5 lakh, and end double taxation of dividends. No explicit calls — no BUY/SELL/HOLD on any ticker and no stock ₹ levels stated. Captions are clean; no garbled spots affect the substance.
